categoryName: Cold beverages — juices, soft drinks, energy drinks, packaged water, mixers

skuLines.examples: Bisleri 1 L, Kinley 500 ml, Aquafina 500 ml, Reliance Campa Sure 1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Apr–Jun peak and again during parents'/visitor season and bus journeys
skuLines.notes: Cheapest freight-per-rupee item in the category, so buy full-truck with the F&V run. At ~1,700 m, winter nights can freeze PET on an unheated verandah and crack/deform it — store inside. Reliance's Campa Sure (₹5/₹15-a-litre entry) has reset the entry price; PET/cap input costs rose through 2026 on West Asia supply disruption, so expect ₹2–5 MRP creep. Sun-exposed stock develops off-taste — keep out of daylight.

skuLines.line: Packaged drinking water — family can 2 L / 5 L / 10 L
skuLines.examples: Bisleri 2 L / 5 L / 10 L, Kinley 2 L, Bailley 10 L, Clear Water 6 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes when a campus borewell/supply line is disrupted or turbid after heavy monsoon
skuLines.notes: Worst freight economics per rupee of revenue in the whole store — only worth it on a backhaul. Real demand driver here is monsoon turbidity in a hill catchment, not taste. Handles crack on hill-road transit; inspect on receipt.

skuLines.examples: Bisleri 20 L jar, Kinley 20 L, a Sirmaur/Nahan-region local packaged-water brand
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Apr–Jun and exam/convocation season peak
skuLines.notes: The highest-value institutional line here: two canteens, hostel blocks, the university offices, the trust office and guest/parent rooms all need it. Needs a jar-deposit register and a local filler within ~50 km — 20 L jars cannot economically be hauled from a plains bottler. Verify the filler's BIS/ISI 14543 licence; jar-water is the most commonly adulterated line in hill districts.

skuLines.examples: Himalayan Natural Mineral Water 1 L, Bisleri Vedica 500 ml/1 L, Catch Still 500 ml, Himalayan Sparkling 750 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks at convocation, donor/trustee visits and international-guest events
skuLines.notes: Stock a shallow depth (2–3 SKUs) purely for VIP/trustee/guest hospitality and the clothing-store-side premium shopper. Glass-bottle variants (Catch, Himalayan Sparkling) break on the ghat road — take PET where a choice exists, and never buy glass without a breakage allowance in the freight deal.

skuLines.examples: Bisleri Club Soda 600 ml/750 ml, Kinley Club Soda 750 ml, Lehar Evervess 600 ml, Catch Club Soda 500 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Sep; near-zero Nov–Feb
skuLines.notes: On this campus soda is bought for nimbu-soda, shikanji, jaljeera and as a home remedy for acidity/indigestion — not as an alcohol mixer. Cheap, unsweetened, and taxed at the plain-water rate rather than the 40% sugary-aerated rate, which makes it the most defensible fizzy line in a school-and-university setting. PET only; RGB glass-crate return over 30–50 km of hill road is not workable.

skuLines.examples: Catch Flavoured Water (Lemon-Lime / Peach / Green Apple) 750 ml, Paper Boat Sparkling Water 250 ml/600 ml, Zenzi Sparkling 350 ml, Schweppes zero-calorie sparkling 600 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun
skuLines.notes: Genuinely useful as the zero-sugar fizzy that sidesteps both the 40% GST slab (unsweetened) and the campus junk-food objection. But it is a taught taste — start with 2 SKUs and a single flavour depth; hill campuses convert slowly and this line is the classic dead-stock trap at ₹60 a bottle.

skuLines.examples: Tata Copper+ 500 ml/1 L, Evocus alkaline 500 ml, Alkapuree 350 ml, Glaceau Smartwater 750 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Only Tata Copper+ earns shelf space at scale — it is priced at plain-water parity (₹9/₹18) and the copper claim lands well with an Ayurveda-friendly institution. The ₹80–250 alkaline tier is a 1-SKU curiosity here; do not build depth.

skuLines.examples: Campa Cola 200/250 ml, Coca-Cola 250 ml, Thums Up 250 ml, Pepsi 250/400 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun sharp peak; collapses Nov–Feb in a cold hill climate
skuLines.marginBand: 8–15% on the big two; 20–30% on Campa (trade estimate)
skuLines.notes: COMPLIANCE FIRST: FSSAI's no-junk-food-within-50 m-of-a-school rule and the UGC/state canteen circulars bite directly on a campus that contains a residential school for 5–18s. Site this line at the main store / university-side counter, never at a counter adjoining school blocks, and keep it out of the two canteens. Post-2025 GST reform, sweetened aerated drinks sit in the 40% slab, so ₹ of gross per case is thin on Coke/Pepsi — Campa and other challengers carry roughly double the retailer margin for the same shelf inch.

skuLines.examples: Coca-Cola 750 ml / 2.25 L, Thums Up 1.25 L / 2 L, Pepsi 1.5 L / 2 L, Campa 2 L
skuLines.seasonality: Festival and family-occasion led: gurpurab, Lohri, Baisakhi, birthdays, parents' visiting days; Apr–Jun otherwise
skuLines.notes: Bought by married staff families for guests, not for daily drinking. Thin margin, bulky, and PET carbonate holds only ~4–6 months, so never carry Apr–Jun depth into the Oct–Mar trough — the winter write-off on 2 L PET is the standard hill-store mistake. Two flavours, two sizes is enough.

skuLines.examples: Sprite 750 ml, Limca 250 ml/750 ml, 7Up, Mountain Dew 1.5 L
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun
skuLines.notes: Caffeine-free (unlike cola), which makes it the version to offer where children are the buyer. Same 40% GST slab and same 50 m siting rule. Limca/Sprite 250 ml at ₹20 is the workhorse; skip Mountain Dew's large packs.

skuLines.examples: Fanta 250 ml/750 ml/2.25 L, Mirinda 750 ml, Campa Orange
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun
skuLines.notes: Caffeine-free. One brand, two sizes. Nothing to distinguish it from lemon-lime commercially — carry it for flavour choice, not as a separate bet.

skuLines.examples: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar 300/330/750 ml, Diet Coke 300 ml, Pepsi Black 400 ml, Sprite Zero 750 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun; steadier than full-sugar because the buyer is habitual, not weather-driven
skuLines.notes: Real and growing demand: diabetic and weight-watching teaching staff and elderly residents, and zero-sugar is the fastest-growing carbonate segment in India through 2026 (Diet Coke demand up ~10x off a small base). Caveat: still 40% GST, and the 2026 aluminium-can shortage made canned Diet Coke chronically unavailable — plan on PET. Two SKUs.

skuLines.line: Jeera / masala / banta soda — ₹10 regional tier
skuLines.examples: Lahori Zeera 160/250 ml, Coca-Cola Rimzim 250 ml (₹10), Bindu Fizz Jeera Masala 250 ml/600 ml/1 L, Bisleri Limonata 160 ml (₹10), Bombay Banta
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Sep; jaljeera/jeera also sells through the monsoon as a digestive
skuLines.marginBand: 20–35% (trade estimate — the segment's whole distribution proposition)
skuLines.notes: The single best commercial line in this category for this store. Campa and Lahori Zeera together doubled to roughly 15% of the Indian soft-drinks market by 2025–26 by paying retailers roughly double what Coke/Pepsi pay, and ₹10 is exactly the pocket-money price point for 5–18s. Also the most palatable fizzy in an institution: non-cola, caffeine-free, and reads as a traditional masala/nimbu drink rather than a Western soda. Watch shrinkflation — ₹10 fill volumes are being quietly cut, so buy on ₹/ml, not on ₹/bottle.

skuLines.examples: Appy Fizz 175 ml (₹15) / 250 ml / 600 ml / 1 L, Fruits & More apple fizz
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun; also the default 'treat drink' at school functions
skuLines.notes: The one fizzy a warden or house-parent will not object to: caffeine-free, apple-juice-based, and marketed as a fruit drink. Note the tax asymmetry — a carbonated drink WITH fruit juice/pulp is treated far more kindly than a plain sweetened aerated water under the reformed GST schedule, so verify the HSN on the invoice; it materially changes landed cost.

skuLines.examples: Coca-Cola 200/300/330 ml can, Thums Up 250 ml can, Schweppes 300 ml can, Sprite 300 ml can
skuLines.packSizes: 200 ml, 250 ml, 300 ml, 330 ml; 4-, 6- and 8-can multipacks
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun and event-led
skuLines.notes: Deprioritise. Cans dent badly on 30–50 km of hill road (a dented can is unsaleable and non-returnable), India ran short of beverage-grade aluminium through 2026, and the format's premium only pays off in an urban chilled-impulse setting. Multipacks are the only version worth carrying, and only for events.

skuLines.line: Mango fruit drink — small pack (₹10–20 impulse tier)
skuLines.examples: Frooti 125/150/160 ml (₹10), Maaza 125 ml (₹10) / 250 ml, Slice 200 ml, Rasna Jumpin 200 ml
skuLines.packSizes: 125 ml, 150 ml, 160 ml, 200 ml, 250 ml tetra & PET; 10×150 ml multipack ₹90
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round baseline with a hard Mar–Jul peak; the least seasonal of all the fizzy/sweet lines
skuLines.notes: The highest-unit-volume line in the whole cold-beverage category for a population this young — pocket-money priced, ambient-stable, tetra travels the ghat road undamaged, 6–9 month shelf life, no chiller needed. Taxed as a fruit-pulp-based drink (5% slab post-reform), not as an aerated drink at 40%, so it is structurally cheaper to sell than any cola. Stock the multipack for hostel wardens and school tiffin.

skuLines.line: Mango fruit drink — family PET 600 ml – 2.25 L
skuLines.examples: Frooti 600 ml / 1.2 L / 2 L / 2.25 L, Maaza 600 ml / 1.2 L / 1.75 L, Slice 1.75 L
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Jul; also gurpurab/langar and family-function led
skuLines.notes: The staff-family and guest-hospitality format, and the low-GST alternative to a 2 L cola for the same occasion. Prefer this over cola family packs on both margin and institutional fit.

skuLines.examples: Real Fruit Power (Mixed Fruit / Guava / Pomegranate / Apple / Pineapple / Cranberry) 1 L, Tropicana Delight Litchi 1 L, B Natural Guava 1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks in exam season, during illness, and at family visits
skuLines.notes: The backbone juice line: ambient-stable, 6–12 month shelf life, no cold chain, tetra survives the road. For a campus with a dispensary and a lot of children, juice is bought as convalescent food as much as refreshment, which is why it holds up in winter when every carbonate dies. Carry 4–6 flavours; guava and mixed fruit outsell orange in North India.

skuLines.examples: Real Activ 100% Orange / Apple 1 L, Tropicana 100% Orange 1 L, Real Activ 100% Apple 200 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: For health-conscious teaching staff, diabetics (with care) and elderly residents. Two SKUs. Note the 2026 CCPA enforcement against overstated '100%' claims (Storia was fined) — buy only from majors whose labelling will survive an inspection, since this store is the sole outlet and carries the reputational exposure alone.

skuLines.examples: Real Fruit Power 180 ml (₹19–20), Tropicana Delight 180 ml, B Natural 180 ml, Paper Boat Aamras 150/200 ml, 4-/6-/12-pack cases
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; term-time driven rather than weather driven
skuLines.notes: Ideal format for this campus: school tiffin, hostel room stock, exam-hall handouts, dispensary use, and the standard giveaway at every function. Ambient, unbreakable, straw attached, 6–12 months. Buy by the case; the case rate is where the margin is. Not for infants under one year.

skuLines.examples: Minute Maid Pulpy Orange 250 ml / 400 ml / 1 L, Tropicana pulpy
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Jul
skuLines.notes: Distinct enough from mango to earn its own facing — pulp is the whole proposition and mango does not substitute for it. One brand, two sizes. Low-GST fruit-drink slab.

skuLines.examples: 7Up Nimbooz 250 ml (₹15) / 350 ml, Bisleri Limonata 160 ml (₹10) / 600 ml, Paper Boat Nimbu Paani
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun peak; useful through the monsoon as a salt-and-lemon rehydrator
skuLines.notes: The most culturally default cold drink in North India after mango, non-carbonated variants included, and it doubles as a heat/dehydration response for staff working outdoors and on the farm/estate. Cheap, ambient, ₹10–15 entry.

skuLines.line: Traditional Indian RTD — aam panna, jaljeera, jeera, kala khatta, sugarcane
skuLines.examples: Paper Boat Swing Jeera 600 ml, Paper Boat Aam Panna / Jaljeera, Raw Pressery Sugarcane 250 ml, Xotik / Bombay Banta kala khatta
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jul strongly; jaljeera and jeera hold through Aug–Sep as digestives
skuLines.notes: The fastest-moving flavour story in Indian beverages through 2026 and the best cultural fit here — no Western-soda objection, reads as ghar-ka-sharbat, and sells to every cohort including elderly residents who will not touch a cola. Start with jeera and aam panna; keep the premium ₹200+ cold-pressed sugarcane out of it (short chilled shelf life, wrong price point).

skuLines.examples: Storia Tender Coconut Water 200 ml / 1 L, Real Activ Coconut Water 1 L, Paper Boat Swing Coconut 1.2 L, Raw Pressery Coconut 200 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jul; also year-round for illness/recovery and post-natal use
skuLines.notes: Fresh tender coconut cannot reach Baru Sahib in usable condition, so packaged is the only option and demand is real — recovery drink, post-natal and post-fever use among staff families, and a genuine electrolyte source. Buy ambient tetra, not the chilled-only SKUs. Note the 2026 CCPA penalty on Storia over '100% tender coconut water' claims — check the current label wording before you commit to a case buy.

skuLines.examples: Raw Pressery Valencia Orange / Alphonso Mango / Pomegranate / Mixed Fruit, 200–250 ml and 1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, guest- and visitor-led
skuLines.notes: Deprioritise or skip. HPP cold-pressed needs an unbroken 4 °C chain and holds only 21–45 days — a 30–50 km hill run and a single chiller make the spoilage risk unacceptable at ₹234–421 a litre. If it is carried at all, take 200/250 ml only, 1 case, for trustee and donor hospitality.

skuLines.examples: Patanjali Amla Juice, Kapiva Wild Amla 1 L, Dabur Giloy/Amla, Baidyanath karela-jamun, Kapiva Dia Free
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Oct–Feb immunity peak and post-illness
skuLines.notes: Strong fit for a Sikh/Ayurveda-friendly institution with an older staff and retiree population: amla, giloy, aloe and diabetic-support juices sell on health belief, not on weather, so this is one of very few cold-beverage lines that holds up through a hill winter. Long ambient shelf life, no chiller. Patanjali gives the best margin and the best price ladder; keep Kapiva to one hero SKU.

skuLines.examples: Hamdard Rooh Afza 750 ml (₹160) / 250 ml, Ganesh Sharbat Kesar Elaichi 700 ml, Gulab sharbat
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Aug hard peak; near-zero Nov–Feb
skuLines.notes: The cheapest cold drink per glass in the store (a 750 ml bottle makes 25–30 glasses at roughly ₹5–6 each) which is exactly what a 5,000-person residential campus and two canteens need in May. Ambient, 18–24 month shelf life, glass bottles need careful packing on the ghat road. Buy the summer's whole requirement in March–April in one freight lot.

skuLines.examples: Kissan Juicy Orange Squash 750 ml, Mala's Blackcurrant Crush 750 ml, Ganesh Mango Panna Squash 700 ml, Mapro Crush, Rasna Mango Power Squash 600 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Aug
skuLines.notes: Canteen and staff-quarter kitchen line: dilute-at-home economics beat every RTD. Orange, lemon and mango-panna cover 80% of demand; the ₹300+ Mapro/Manama premium crushes are for the F&V juice counter, not the shelf. Sharbats sit at a lower GST rate than aerated drinks — another reason to push concentrate over cola.

skuLines.examples: Rasna Fruit Fun 20 g sachet (₹50, makes 32 glasses), Rasna Nagpur Orange, Tang Orange/Lemon/Mango 17.2 g (₹5) / 75 g (₹26) / 500 g (₹150) / 750 g (₹249)
skuLines.packSizes: 15–20 g single sachet, 75 g, 250 g, 500 g, 750 g, 2×500 g
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Aug peak; the 500 g/750 g jars sell to canteens year-round
skuLines.notes: Lowest cost per glass of anything in the category and the best freight economics in the store — a 750 g Tang jar is 30+ litres of drink in 750 g of freight, versus 30 kg of PET for the same litres up 40 km of hill road. Two buying jobs in one line: the ₹5 sachet for school children's pocket money, and the 500 g/750 g jar on a monthly canteen indent. Ambient, 12–18 months, no chiller.

skuLines.examples: Nestea Lemon 400 g / 750 g, Wagh Bakri Lemon & Peach Ice Tea 250/400 g, Continental Lemon 140/400 g, Tata Tea Gold instant iced tea sachets 130 g
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Aug
skuLines.notes: Bought by the two canteens and the Ary Lite counter, not by households — it is a service input. Tea concentrates sit outside the 40% aerated slab. Take one lemon and one peach in the 400 g size and the ₹100 sachet pack for retail trial; skip the ₹250–600 specialty tins.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Hommade Lemoneez 250 ml (₹85), Keya Lemon Juice 250/500 ml, ReaLemon-type
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Apr–Jul peak
skuLines.notes: Sits across cold beverages and the kitchen shelf — shikanji and nimbu-soda in summer, cooking and warm nimbu-pani in winter, which makes it one of the few lines with no seasonal trough. Fresh lemons are expensive and irregular this far up a hill road, which strengthens the case. Refrigerate after opening.

skuLines.examples: Shree Guruji Kesaria Thandai 500 ml, Hitkary Sandali Brahmi Badam 750 ml, Ganesh Khus/Blue Curacao sharbat, Mapro Lounge sharbat 250 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Holi/Baisakhi and Apr–Jun; badam-milk syrup also sells Oct–Feb as a warm drink
skuLines.notes: Festival line — buy against a named date (Baisakhi, Holi, gurpurab langar), not as standing stock, or it sits a full year. Badam/thandai syrup is the exception: it converts to a hot milk drink and therefore sells through a hill winter.

skuLines.examples: Electral 21.8 g sachet, ORSL WHO-ORS ready-to-drink, Prolyte ORS, Walyte
skuLines.packSizes: 4.4 g, 21.8 g sachet; strip of 5/10; 200 ml RTD
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks Apr–Jun (heat) and Jul–Sep (monsoon diarrhoea season); needed year-round
skuLines.notes: The one non-negotiable line in this whole category. A closed township with ~5,000 residents including babies, small children and a residential school, 30–50 km from the nearest hospital or real pharmacy, cannot be out of stock of WHO-formula ORS during a monsoon gastro outbreak. Stock ONLY true WHO-ORS: FSSAI ordered all sugary drinks branded as 'ORS' pulled from shelves and the Delhi High Court upheld it in 2026, and the paediatric bodies are explicit that electrolyte/fruit drinks are not a substitute. 24–36 month shelf life, near-zero freight weight — carry 4+ weeks of cover and coordinate the level with the campus dispensary.

skuLines.examples: ORSL / ORSL Advanz Care 200 ml, Enerzal RTD, eRZL, Rebalanz
skuLines.packSizes: 200 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml; 1 kg powder jar
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun and Jul–Sep
skuLines.notes: For adults, sports and mild dehydration — explicitly NOT the treatment line; keep it physically separated from the WHO-ORS facing so nobody buys it for a dehydrated infant. Kenvue's 2026 dual-brand split (ORSL for non-diarrhoeal hydration, eRZL and RTD WHO-ORS for diarrhoeal) is precisely this distinction, and getting it wrong is the live regulatory risk in this category right now.

skuLines.examples: Glucon-D Tangy Orange 75 g (₹49) / 400 g / 450 g / 1 kg, Dextrose/Glucose-C, Glucovita
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jul peak; year-round for fever, fasting and exam season
skuLines.notes: Cheap, ambient, 18–24 months, weightless relative to its litres, and used here for three separate jobs: heat exhaustion, recovery during fever, and energy on treks and sports days at altitude. Also the drink of choice during religious fasts. Stock the ₹49 small pack for students and the 1 kg jar for the canteens and dispensary.

skuLines.examples: Gatorade 250 ml (₹20) / 500 ml (₹50) in Orange / Lemon / Blue Bolt, Enerzal RTD, Prime Hydration (premium)
skuLines.seasonality: Sports season, gurmat/summer camps, inter-college meets; Mar–Jun
skuLines.notes: Eternal University sport and the school's athletics programme are the demand. Gatorade's ₹20/250 ml zero-sugar pack is the right entry — it clears the sugary-drink objection and hits a student price point. Skip Prime Hydration at ₹399; it is influencer-priced and will not turn here.

skuLines.examples: Sting 180 ml (₹30) / 500 ml, Red Bull 250 ml, Monster Ultra 350 ml, Hell Energy 250 ml, Cloud 9
skuLines.seasonality: Exam season peaks; Apr–Jun
skuLines.notes: Handle as a policy decision, not a buying decision. FSSAI issued a 90-day order in 2026 stripping the 'energy drink' descriptor — these must now be sold as caffeinated beverages, are capped at 300 mg/L caffeine, and carry a 'not recommended for children' warning. On a campus whose largest cohort is 5–18-year-olds, and under the UGC/state junk-food circulars, the defensible position is: stock at most 1–2 SKUs, at the university-side counter only, never at any counter near the school or in either canteen, and never in the ₹30 pocket-money format that children can buy. Also the 40% GST slab.

skuLines.examples: Aquatein Pro protein water 500 ml, Parag/Avvatar milk-protein RTD, Yoga Bar protein shake, whey-isolate protein water
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; gym-cycle driven
skuLines.notes: Fastest-growing functional segment in India in 2026 and a real fit for university students using the campus gym, but it is a 1–2 SKU trial at this scale, and the dairy-protein versions need a chiller. Watch the 2026 whey supply squeeze — pricing on imported-whey SKUs is unstable, so do not lock a large case buy.

skuLines.line: Electrolyte drink mix sachets — kids & trek
skuLines.examples: Sweetmate electrolyte mix 50 g (Lemon-Lime / Mango / Orange), Fast&Up Reload, Nutriburst hydration tablets
skuLines.packSizes: 4–10 g sachet, 50 g pack, effervescent tube of 10/20
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun and trek/camp season
skuLines.notes: Powder format, so freight is negligible and shelf life long — the attraction is that it stores where an RTD cannot. Must be merchandised away from the ORS facing and must not be described as ORS, per the 2026 FSSAI order. One or two SKUs.

skuLines.examples: Amul Masti Spiced Buttermilk 200 ml (₹15) / 1 L, Mother Dairy Masala Chach 180 ml, Verka chaas, Amul Probiotic Buttermilk 180 ml (₹10), Amul Chaas polypack 400 ml
skuLines.packSizes: 180 ml, 200 ml, 250 ml, 400 ml pouch, 500 ml, 1 L
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Aug peak; steady year-round with meals
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the dairy lane — flag it there too, but it belongs on the cold-beverage chiller commercially. For a North Indian institutional population this is the default cold drink with a meal, and at ₹10–15 it beats every packaged soft drink on both price and acceptability. UHT tetra holds 60–180 days ambient until opened; pouch chaas is 2–5 days chilled and should not be bought at all unless the chiller is reliable. Verka (Punjab Milkfed) is the culturally native brand here and worth prioritising over Amul on that alone.

skuLines.examples: Amul Lassi 200 ml (₹15) / Rose 250 ml / Mango 1 L, Verka Sweet Lassi 200 ml, Mother Dairy Lassi Sweet/Mango 180 ml, Amul Sugar Free Lassi 180 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Aug peak; holds better through winter than any carbonate
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the dairy lane. Highest-frequency sweet cold drink for this population and the closest packaged equivalent to what a Punjabi household actually drinks. Carry sweet, rose and mango, plus the sugar-free SKU for diabetic staff. Taxed in the 5% slab as a milk beverage. Needs chiller space — this and chaas should get first claim on it, ahead of carbonates.

skuLines.examples: Amul Kool (Kesar / Rose / Badam / Elaichi / Chocolate) 180–200 ml, Verka flavoured milk, Britannia Winkin Cow 180 ml, Cavin's, Osam Kesar Elaichi 180 ml (₹30)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round — the one cold-beverage line that grows in a hill winter because it is drunk warm too
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the dairy lane. The single best line to lean on for the 5–18 cohort: parents and wardens approve it, it clears every junk-food rule, it is in the 5% GST slab, and unlike every carbonate it does not die in October. Ambient UHT tetra keeps 90–180 days, so it does not compete for chiller space unless sold chilled. Kesar-badam and chocolate outsell the rest.

skuLines.examples: Amul Kool Cafe 180/200 ml, Hershey's milkshake 200 ml, Cavin's cold coffee, Paper Boat Chill Coffee
skuLines.seasonality: Mar–Jul; exam-season late-night demand year-round
skuLines.notes: University-cohort line, and the acceptable caffeine format for a campus that should be cautious with energy drinks — a cold coffee has a fraction of the caffeine and none of the labelling problem. 2–3 SKUs at the university-side counter and Ary Lite.

skuLines.examples: Lipton Ice Tea Lemon 250 ml (₹50) / 350 ml, Honest Tea Organic Green Mango 350 ml, Brewhouse Organic Peach 350 ml, Bevvy Lemon 250 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jul
skuLines.notes: Non-carbonated, low-caffeine, and reads as a tea rather than a soft drink, which makes it easy to place anywhere on campus. Lipton at ₹50 is the volume SKU; the ₹80–120 unsweetened craft tier (Teafit, Brewhouse) is a 1-SKU experiment. Cheaper to serve from premix at the canteens — do not let the RTD cannibalise that.

skuLines.examples: Tetley Kombucha 265 ml, RTB Kombucha 250 ml, Neer Kombucha, Local Ferment Co.
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Probably skip. Live-culture products need continuous refrigeration (they can over-carbonate and burst if the chain breaks on a warm hill run), the price point is ₹100+, and awareness among this population is close to zero. Revisit only if the premium tier of the staff cohort actually asks.

skuLines.examples: Dr Cubes 1 kg, Dras Ice 500 g / 1 kg, Ice Craft 1 kg pouch, Rock Ice Gourmet 1 kg
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Jun only
skuLines.notes: Do not buy packaged ice — it needs a dedicated deep freezer, melts in transit over 30–50 km, and in a cold hill climate the season is 8–10 weeks. If the canteens or the F&V juice counter need ice for shikanji and lassi, make it on site from a small cube machine; that is the economic answer here, not a bought SKU.

skuLines.examples: Schweppes Indian Tonic Water 300 ml, Sepoy & Co Ginger Ale / Elderflower Tonic 200 ml, Jimmy's Tonic 600 ml, Bacardi Mixr non-alcoholic mixers, Catch Ginger Ale 200 ml
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, event-led
skuLines.notes: Almost entirely inappropriate here and should mostly be skipped. Tonic water, cocktail mixers and anything beer-branded (Barbican, Budweiser 0.0, 'non-alcoholic beer') exist to imitate alcohol service and have no place in a Kalgidhar Trust township where alcohol and tobacco are prohibited — carrying them would read as an institutional error regardless of the ABV. If a mixer facing is wanted at all, keep it to plain club soda and a ginger ale, both sold on their own merits. Ginger ale genuinely helps nausea on hill journeys, which is the one honest argument for it.

skuLines.examples: Case lots of Real 180 ml (12/24), Frooti 10×150 ml, Maaza 150 ml tetra cases, Bisleri 500 ml ×24, Coca-Cola 8×250 ml, Amul Kool 200 ml cases

skuLines.notes: A distinct buying job, not just a pack size: on a campus of 5,000 with a school, a university and a trust that runs functions, the beverage requirement arrives as an indent for 500–3,000 units against a date. Negotiate a standing case rate with the distributor, plan a 3–4 week lead time because the Sirmaur hill roads can close in the monsoon, and default to ambient tetra and PET — nothing that needs a chiller or that breaks. This is where scale pricing and a large share of the category's absolute rupees actually sit.

trends2026: GST reform reshuffled the whole category's economics: sweetened aerated waters, carbonated fruit drinks and caffeinated beverages sit in the new 40% 'sin goods' slab, while fruit-pulp/juice-based drinks, beverages containing milk, soya milk drinks and pre-packed lassi/buttermilk sit at 5% and plain unsweetened mineral/sparkling water at 18%. Juice-based, dairy-based and plain-water lines are now structurally cheaper to sell than any cola — the single most decision-relevant fact in this category for 2026.

The ₹10 challenger tier broke the 30-year Coke-Pepsi duopoly: Reliance's Campa and Lahori Zeera together roughly doubled to ~15% of the Indian soft-drinks market by 2025-26, built on paying retailers roughly double the incumbent margin. Coca-Cola answered with Rimzim at ₹10/250 ml and Bisleri with Limonata at ₹10/160 ml. Watch shrinkflation — ₹10 fill volumes are being quietly cut, so buy on ₹/ml.

FSSAI issued a 90-day order stripping the 'energy drink' descriptor — Red Bull, Sting, Monster and the rest must relabel as 'caffeinated beverage', stay under 300 mg/L caffeine, and carry a not-recommended-for-children warning. On a campus whose largest cohort is 5-18, this converts an assortment question into a policy question.

The ORS crackdown: FSSAI ordered every sugary drink branded as 'ORS' pulled from shops and e-commerce, the Delhi High Court upheld it, and the paediatric bodies backed it hard. Real WHO-formula ORS and 'hydration' drinks are now legally and clinically distinct lines that must be merchandised apart — Kenvue split its own portfolio (ORSL for non-diarrhoeal hydration, eRZL and RTD WHO-ORS for diarrhoeal) to match.

Zero-sugar went mainstream rather than niche: Diet Coke demand rose roughly 10x off a small base, and regional players are now launching no-sugar variants on the health hook rather than leaving it to the multinationals. Zero-sugar is also the fastest-growing carbonate segment and the version that survives the junk-food objection.

Hydration and electrolytes emerged as a category in their own right, separate from both sports drinks and medicine — Gatorade pushed a ₹20/250 ml zero-sugar entry pack, Kenvue ran a dual-brand hydration play, and botanical/electrolyte powder mixes for kids proliferated.

Traditional Indian flavours became the innovation engine — jeera/zeera, aam panna, jaljeera, kala khatta, nimbu, sugarcane, kokum and packaged coconut water are where the growth and the new entrants are (Lahori Zeera, Bombay Banta, Paper Boat Swing, Rasna's Jumpin expansion). CCPA fined Storia over '100% tender coconut water' claims, so label diligence now matters on this tier.

Input-cost and packaging shocks moved retail prices: West Asia supply disruption pushed PET resin and cap costs up, packaged-water MRPs rose ₹5-10 in several markets and 20 L jar rates went up, and a beverage-grade aluminium shortage left canned SKUs (notably Diet Coke) chronically unavailable through 2026 — plan on PET and tetra, not cans.

Regulatory pressure on sales near education campuses tightened: the FSSAI no-junk-food-within-50-m-of-a-school rule, UGC and AICTE circulars against junk food in college canteens, and fresh state-level bans (Maharashtra, Karnataka) all bear directly on a retail outlet sited inside a residential school and university township.

Protein and functional RTD moved from gyms into general trade — protein water with whey isolate plus electrolytes, and milk-protein RTDs from mainstream dairies — though a 2026 global whey supply squeeze made pricing on imported-whey SKUs unstable.
adjacentServices: 20 L jar and chilled-water delivery on a subscription to hostel blocks, staff quarters, the university offices, the trust office and guest/parent rooms — with a jar-deposit register and a return round; the highest-value recurring service attachable to this category

Brand-funded visi-cooler / chiller placement: Coca-Cola, PepsiCo and Campa are in an aggressive fridge-placement war in India, so chiller capacity — the binding physical constraint on cold beverages in a hill store — can be obtained as a trade investment rather than capex, at each of the POS store, the two canteens, the F&V counter and Ary Lite

Event and langar beverage supply as a quoted service: a standing case-rate card and a 3-4 week indent calendar for gurpurab, Baisakhi, sports day, annual function, convocation, parents' day, admission season and summer camps
Monthly canteen indent for premix, squash, sharbat and concentrate — a service contract on inputs rather than counter retail, and the best ₹-per-kg-of-freight in the whole category

A fresh shikanji / nimbu-soda / lassi / seasonal-fruit-juice counter run off the existing fruits-and-vegetables counter, consuming squash, lemon concentrate, sharbat and on-site ice: converts a low-margin concentrate SKU into a high-margin served drink and captures the summer demand that packaged drinks lose in a cold climate

A monsoon-and-heat rehydration kit — WHO-ORS sachets plus glucose powder plus a small still-water bottle — stocked and level-set jointly with the campus dispensary, so a 5,000-person closed township 30-50 km from a hospital is never out of ORS during a gastro outbreak
On-site ice production (a small cube machine) for the canteens and juice counter instead of buying packaged ice that melts on the ghat road

Empty PET and tetra collection / segregated recycling with a small buy-back, which both meets Himachal's plastic-waste expectations for a closed township and creates a reason for residents to return to the store

Diabetic and elderly-resident 'safe drinks' shelf — zero-sugar carbonate, unsweetened iced tea, 100% juice, sugar-free lassi, amla and karela-jamun juice — curated with the dispensary as an advisory service rather than a pure assortment
